title: Daily Market Briefing
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Metals liquidation, oil bid, hawkish Fed repricing.
Silver's -4.23% and gold's -1.80% led a broad risk-off session, yet WTI +3.30% and UUP +0.60% show this was a dollar/real-rate story, not a growth scare. With Curves steepening, TLT -1.58%, and FedWatch pricing 100% hike odds at the Oct 28 FOMC, the tape is repricing tightening into an already narrow market (only 28% of S&P 500 above 50-DMA).

INDICES — VIX 14.2, below its 20-day MA of 15.6 — complacency despite the sell-off.
Ranking: SPY -0.72%, QQQ -0.84%, DIA -0.71%, IWM -1.84%, SOXX -1.23%. Small < large by 0.40pp (IWM -1.84% vs SPY -0.72% — note STYLE line uses IJR -1.12%).
Most notable cross-asset move: SLV -4.23%, a precious-metals liquidation.
SPY and QQQ remain above 200-DMA, so no CTA sell trigger yet — but only 46% of S&P 500 members are above theirs.

VOLUME & BREADTH — SPY vol_ratio 1.3x, QQQ 0.9x — SPY volume elevated on a down day = distribution; QQQ light volume down = no conviction either way.
SOXX 1.4x and IJH 1.4x gaining attention; SLV 0.9x, IJR 0.8x, GLD 0.7x being ignored.
Breadth diverges badly: 168/332 adv/dec, up/down vol ratio 0.39, only 28% above 50-DMA, 13 new highs vs 105 new lows — participation is failing the index-level resilience. This is a narrow mega-cap tape masking broad internal weakness.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLI Industrials +0.00%, XLF Financials +0.00%, XLE Energy +0.00%, XLP Staples -0.36%, XLK Technology -0.47%, XLB Materials -0.49%, XLV Healthcare -0.64%, XLC Comms -0.85%, XLY Discretionary -1.50%, XLRE Real Estate -1.55%, XLU Utilities -1.92%.
Top industries: USO +3.30%, MSOS +1.88%; bottom: XBI -4.12%, GDX -4.36%, SILJ -5.44%.
Sector flows: XLY +$711mm (100th pct) and XLK +$147mm lead inflows; XLF -$2,305mm (0th pct), XLV -$1,089mm, XLE -$890mm bleed hardest — flows CONTRADICT the flat price ranking, with the biggest outflow sectors (XLF) not the worst performers, suggesting mechanical de-risking rather than conviction selling.
